product_rules: no session-length input; the plan is sized by exercise count; time is an estimate (R4-SES-01, R4-SES-02)
two days a week: every big group at about 6-8 weekly sets, a third day suggested (R4-SES-03)

optional add-ons, carries by distance or time, mid-range pull, incline first, swap notes, search-only video links (R4-LIB-01..05)
everyone may use it; the terms and release accepted before a plan is generated; a release line on every plan; a confidence label on every sport profile (R4-SCP-01..03)

4 exercises fixed for the exercise block: filter (kit, soft level, population rules incl. EQ-03, 60+ and racket-50+ defaults with their switches, pain with rotation-bias swaps, exclusions), default pick + same-category dropdown; second weekly exposure different and non-axial on the non-spine day; one-detail changes between exercise blocks, never an invented exercise (COACH-R2 R2-LIB-01); v1.3: optional add-ons are never picked (wall balls and sled pushes in a HYROX circuit or the class WOD excepted; R4-LIB-01); incline before overhead in the vertical / mid-range push slot for muscle, general, fat-loss and stay-active goals (R4-LIB-03); every swap and every stand-in carries a keeps / loses line (R4-LIB-04); video = a YouTube search link + the exact name to copy (R4-LIB-05)

6 the whole plan at once (no deload or maintenance inside a block; no check-in, no feedback, COACH-R3 R3-VOL-02 / R3-VOL-04): every trained group follows its stairway from start to its planned final sets (pattern ~3 % to halfway, ~5 % after, x lambda, lambda free; the final sets ARE reached, in the last week or one week early at most; COACH-CX CX-01, COACH-R4 R4-PRG-01); weeks that add more than about 15 % are noted (R4-PRG-02); the week's sets are split over the template slots (VOL-07 order, the two exposures of a day type alternating, 2-5 sets an exercise); no room -> the bonus exercise on the optional day, else the group is capped and the plan says so (R4-SES-04); a group at its final sets keeps them while reps and load progress (CX-02, CX-03); superset suggestions between neighbouring pairs (the person switches them on); each day carries exercise_count, est_minutes and the easy-to-remove hints. effort.how_hard.en: How heavy? Each exercise tells you how many reps to leave in the tank: "leave 2 in the tank" means you could do 2 more reps at the end of the set (about RPE 8; 3 left = RPE 7, 1 left = RPE 9). Your plan starts with 3 in the tank, then 2, then 1-2, and in the last week 1 with a few extra-hard sets. Week 1: start a little lighter, with a weight you could lift 2-3 more times.
effort.how_hard.es: ¿Cuánto peso? Cada ejercicio te dice cuántas repeticiones dejar en reserva: "deja 2 en reserva" significa que podrías hacer 2 repeticiones más al final de la serie (aproximadamente RPE 8; 3 en reserva = RPE 7, 1 en reserva = RPE 9). Tu plan empieza con 3 en reserva, luego 2, luego 1-2, y en la última semana 1 con algunas series extra duras. Semana 1: empieza un poco más ligero, con un peso que podrías levantar 2-3 veces más.

effort.olympic.en: Olympic lifts are for power. Cleans, snatches and their dumbbell and kettlebell versions train power: move the weight as fast as you can with clean technique. Pick a weight you can move explosively on every rep; if it slows down or your technique breaks, it's too heavy. You don't need percentages for these unless you compete in Olympic weightlifting.
effort.olympic.es: Los levantamientos olímpicos son para la potencia. Las cargadas (cleans), las arrancadas (snatches) y sus versiones con mancuernas y kettlebells entrenan potencia: mueve el peso lo más rápido que puedas con buena técnica. Elige un peso que puedas mover de forma explosiva en cada repetición; si se frena o se rompe la técnica, es demasiado pesado. No necesitas porcentajes para estos levantamientos, a menos que compitas en halterofilia (Olympic weightlifting).
